page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the n1-standard-8 delivers modest processing capabilities. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the weak category (bottom 25%), with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the poor tier (bottom 10%). However, memory subsystem performance is more resilient; while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths achieve average ratings (middle 50%). Passmark memory scores and LLM text generation speeds for small models also demonstrate average performance, whereas database operations and static web serving throughput remain in the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-standard-8 offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for legacy general-purpose workloads that do not require high-frequency compute or rapid cryptographic processing. The absence of local NVMe storage and weak single-core execution speeds represent significant tradeoffs, making it less efficient for intensive database operations or high-throughput web serving. It is best utilized for moderate general-purpose tasks, basic software compilation, or lightweight background processing where memory capacity is prioritized over raw CPU throughput.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 30.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the lower tiers, with single-core and multi-core CPU metrics, static web serving, and database operations scoring in the bottom 25%. However, it maintains average performance in large-block memory bandwidth and small-model LLM text generation. Given these performance tradeoffs, the n1-standard-8 is best suited for moderate general-purpose workloads, basic software development tasks, and memory-reliant applications that do not demand high-frequency CPU execution or local NVMe storage.
